title: Low-total-degree moments have a large arbitrary-weight kernel on the Phi6 union, but degree one separates the structured Phi6 rows
mathematical_status: proved linear-algebra and finite-difference kill test with an exact signed certificate; not a Euclidean or structured-divisor no-go

setup.phi6_union: For d>=2 and k=floor(d/2), U consists of exponent vectors (y,x_1,...,x_d) with y in {0,1}, x_i in {0,1,2}, and at most k nonzero x_i. Thus R=|U|=2 sum_(s=0)^k binom(d,s)2^s.
setup.moment_map: For a rational signed weight w on U and multiindex alpha, m_alpha(w)=sum_(u in U)w(u)u^alpha. Let M_L retain every alpha of total degree |alpha|<=L.
setup.feature_count: There are F(d,L)=binom(d+1+L,L) formal monomials in d+1 variables of total degree at most L. Polynomial relations on U can only lower the evaluation rank, so rank(M_L)<=F(d,L).

kernel_lower_bound.fixed_L: For every fixed L, F(d,L)=Theta(d^L) while R=2^(3d/2-o(d)); hence dim ker(M_L)=R(1-o(1)).
kernel_lower_bound.logarithmic_L: For L<=C log d with fixed C, log F<=L log(e(d+1+L)/L)=O((log d)^2)=o(d), while log R=(3/2+o(1))d log 2. Hence again dim ker(M_L)=R(1-o(1)).
kernel_lower_bound.interpretation: Both L=O(1) and L=O(log f), with displayed factor count f=d+1, necessarily leave an exponentially large linear kernel on arbitrary signed weights supported in U.

explicit_all_parameter_kernel_vector.definition: Let m=L+1 and, with y and all unused x-coordinates fixed to zero, set mu=product_(i=1)^m(delta_(x_i=1)-delta_(x_i=0)). Its coefficient at the Boolean point 1_S is (-1)^(m-|S|).
explicit_all_parameter_kernel_vector.support_in_U: Every Boolean support point has at most m<=k nonzero x-coordinates, so supp(mu) is contained in U.
explicit_all_parameter_kernel_vector.moment_vanishing: A monomial of total degree at most L has positive exponent in at most L<m of the active coordinates. It misses some active coordinate j, and summation against delta_1-delta_0 in that coordinate is zero. Thus m_alpha(mu)=0 for every |alpha|<=L.
explicit_all_parameter_kernel_vector.positive_negative_split: Writing mu=mu_plus-mu_minus, both mu_plus and mu_minus are 0/1 rows with 2^L atoms and identical total-degree-at-most-L moments. Exactly one of their supports contains the origin. This already gives different support properties invisible to the retained moments.

equal_augmentation_signed_rows.general_construction: For L>=2, let z=(y=1,x_1=...=x_d=0) and define q_plus=mu_plus-(2^L-2)delta_z and q_minus=mu_minus-(2^L-2)delta_z. Both are genuinely signed rational/integer rows supported in U, both have augmentation 2, and all moments of total degree <=L agree because their difference remains mu.
equal_augmentation_signed_rows.different_support_property: Exactly one row contains the origin; their Boolean parts are opposite Hamming-parity classes.

exact_certificate.row_plus: coefficient +1 on the even-cardinality subsets of {x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4}, coefficient -6 at the common y atom, zero elsewhere
exact_certificate.row_minus: coefficient +1 on the odd-cardinality subsets of {x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4}, coefficient -6 at the common y atom, zero elsewhere
exact_certificate.moment_identity: m_alpha(q_plus)=m_alpha(q_minus) for all alpha with total degree <=3
exact_certificate.support_difference: q_plus contains the all-zero exponent vector; q_minus does not

structured_phi6_boundary.degree_one_fingerprint: The constant moment is 2, the Y first moment is 1, and the X_i first moment is 2 if i in A and 0 otherwise.
structured_phi6_boundary.consequence: The labelled total-degree-at-most-one moments already recover A and distinguish all binom(d,k) actual Q_A rows.
structured_phi6_boundary.kill_test_boundary: The large-kernel theorem applies to arbitrary signed weights on the Phi6 union. It does not produce two actual divisor rows Q_A with equal low moments and does not refute a method that exploits their factorized coefficient pattern.

what_is_killed: Universal reconstruction of an arbitrary signed weight on U from all total-degree-at-most-L moments when L=O(1) or O(log f).
Any assertion that a polynomial or quasipolynomial number of low-degree linear moments determines support properties such as origin membership for arbitrary equal-augmentation signed rows on U.
what_is_not_killed: Low-degree tests tailored to the structured Phi6 divisor rows; degree one already distinguishes those rows.
Nonlinear, tensor-compressed, factor-aware, scalar-copy or positivity certificates.
A low-order moment defect theorem whose conclusion is a Euclidean ruled locus rather than complete support reconstruction.
The actual exact-block family, because q_plus and q_minus are not proved to divide B, become masks after the required source multiplications, or arise from scalar copies of one Euclidean source.
scope_and_closure.euclidean_status: The certificate lives only in the abstract exponent-support union. It is not an N-point Euclidean configuration, supplies no distance-label count, and is not a counterexample to Erdős #1083.

next_legal_attempt: Use the actual factorized coefficient fingerprints and scalar-copy/positive-multiple constraints. A viable low-degree invariant must exploit relations among rows or imply a bounded-degree Euclidean ruled locus; arbitrary-weight support reconstruction is now frozen.

bounded_guard.result: Exact parity certificates passed for 4<=d<=12 and every 0<=L<floor(d/2); the d=8,L=3 equal-augmentation signed certificate passed; degree-one fingerprints were distinct for all structured Phi6 rows through d=10; dimension ledgers passed through d=256.
